description: A software development team is tasked with building a highly concurrent, distributed caching service that must adhere to stringent performance and security requirements. The goal is to design, implement, and test a solution that can handle millions of requests per second while protecting sensitive data. The team consists of an Architect, a Senior Backend Engineer, a Security Engineer, a DevOps Specialist, and a Quality Assurance Lead. The Architect provides the high-level design. The Senior Backend Engineer implements the core logic. The Security Engineer reviews and hardens the system. The DevOps Specialist deploys and monitors the service. The Quality Assurance Lead designs test cases and verifies functionality. A critical, non-negotiable constraint is that the cache eviction policy must be 'Least Recently Used' (LRU) with an exact maximum capacity of 500,000 entries. Additionally, all data at rest within the cache must be encrypted using AES-256 GCM. The fully connected topology ensures every agent can directly communicate with any other agent, facilitating immediate information exchange crucial for maintaining consistency and adherence to these complex, intertwined constraints in a hard-structural-complexity scenario, with an expected 28 turns to fully explore design and implementation details.

ground_truth.correct_outcome: The team successfully designs, implements, deploys, and tests a caching service that strictly adheres to the 'Least Recently Used' (LRU) eviction policy with an exact maximum capacity of 500,000 entries. Furthermore, all data at rest within the cache is verified to be encrypted using AES-256 GCM. All agents consistently communicate and implement these specific technical and security constraints throughout the design, development, and testing phases.
ground_truth.quality_rubric: Score 0-100: LRU eviction policy correctly implemented (30 pts), exact maximum capacity of 500,000 entries maintained (30 pts), AES-256 GCM encryption for data at rest fully integrated and verified (30 pts), overall design coherence and performance considerations (10 pts).
